9x18 mm PST Ammo
9x18 mm Ammo
The 9x18 PST cartridge (GRAU/GAU index 57-N-181S) is a standard Soviet pistol round with a steel-core bullet, adopted in 1956 for the Makarov pistol (PM) and the Stechkin automatic pistol (APS). It replaced the earlier lead-core P cartridge, offering easier production and improved penetration.\n \n
9x18 mm SP8 Ammo
The 9x18 SP8 cartridge (special-purpose cartridge, GRAU index 7N1`) is a special pistol round with a low-penetration expanding bullet. It was developed in 1989 by TsNIITochMash for law-enforcement and counter-terrorism units.\n \n
9x18 mm PMM Ammo
The 9x18 PMM cartridge (GAU/GRAU index 57-N-181SM, code 7N16) is a modernized Soviet high-power pistol round. It was developed in the late 1980s for the modernized Makarov pistol (PMM) and submachine guns such as the Klin and Bizon, with the aim of penetrating light body armor.
9x18 mm RG028 Ammo
The 9x18 mm RG028 gzh cartridge (GRAU index RG028) is a Soviet special-purpose pistol round with increased penetration. It was developed in the late 1970s by TsNIITochMash specialists at the request of the USSR KGB for use in the standard Makarov pistol (PM).
9x18 mm PBM Ammo
The 9x18 PBM cartridge (GRAU index 7N25) is a special Russian pistol round with an enhanced armor-piercing bullet. It was developed in the late 1990s by the Instrument Design Bureau in Tula for standard 9x18 mm PM weapons such as the PM and PB pistols, allowing effective engagement of targets wearing body armor at ranges up to 50 meters.
9x18 mm PPT Ammo
The 9 PPT gzh cartridge (GAU index 57-T-181) is a special 9x18 mm pistol round with a tracer bullet. It was designed by V. V. Trunov and P. F. Sazonov for target indication, fire correction, and combat in poor visibility.
9x19 mm FMJ Ammo
9x19 mm Ammo
The 9x19 FMJ (Full Metal Jacket) cartridge is one of the world's most common standard 9x19 mm Parabellum pistol rounds, using a fully jacketed bullet. It is widely used for sport, training, self-defense, and military purposes.
9x19 mm T Ammo
The 9x19 T cartridge (GRAU index 7T4) is an experimental Soviet pistol round with a tracer bullet, developed by TsNIITochMash. It was intended for target indication and fire correction from submachine guns and other 9x19 mm weapons, but it was not adopted and never entered serial production.
9x19 mm PBP Ammo
The 9x19 PBP cartridge (enhanced armor-piercing bullet, GRAU index 7N31) is a Russian combat round. It was developed in the early 2000s by KBP in Tula to defeat personnel wearing body armor up to roughly class 2-3 at distances up to 50 meters.
9x19 mm +P Ammo
9x19 mm cartridges marked +P (Plus Pressure) and +P+ are loaded to higher pressure than standard ammunition. The increased gas pressure gives the bullet greater velocity and stopping power, but requires a firearm designed to withstand the additional stress.
9x19 mm AP Ammo
The 9x19 AP cartridge, often known as AP 6.3, is a semi-armor-piercing 9x19 mm Parabellum pistol round. It is specialized ammunition intended to improve effectiveness against personal body armor.
9x19 mm RIP Ammo
9x19 mm RIP is ammunition designed for maximum terminal effect through bullet fragmentation after impact.
7.62x25 mm P Ammo
7.62x25 mm Ammo
The 7.62x25 P cartridge (GAU/GRAU index 57-N-132) is a Soviet 7.62x25 mm pistol cartridge with a standard lead-core bullet designated P. It was adopted together with the TT pistol in 1930.
7.62x25 mm PT Ammo
The 7.62x25 PT cartridge (GAU index 57-T-133) is a Soviet pistol round with a tracer bullet, developed for the TT pistol and PPD, PPSh, and PPS submachine guns. The designation PT means pistol tracer.
7.62x25 mm PS Ammo
The Soviet 7.62x25 PS pistol cartridge (GRAU index 57-N-134S for steel/bimetal cases or 57-N-132S for brass cases) is a centerfire 7.62x25 mm TT round with a steel-core bullet. It was adopted in the USSR in 1953 to replace earlier lead-core bullets.
7.62x25 mm P-41 Ammo
The Soviet 7.62x25 mm cartridge with the P-41 armor-piercing incendiary bullet (GAU index 57-BZ-132) was adopted in 1941. It was produced throughout the Second World War and intended to damage lightly armored vehicles, motorcycles, cars, and ignite fuel tanks.
5.7x28 mm SS190 Ammo
5.7x28 mm Ammo
The 5.7x28 mm SS190 cartridge is the standard 5.7x28 mm round with a steel and aluminum core. FN Herstal developed it for PDW weapons such as the FN P90 submachine gun and FN Five-seveN pistol to penetrate light body armor.
5.7x28 mm L191 Ammo
The 5.7x28 mm L191 is an armor-piercing tracer round developed by FN Herstal. Its 2.1-gram bullet has a heat-treated steel tip and aluminum core in a copper jacket, with tracer compound in the rear that leaves a visible blue trail in flight. The bullet tip is painted red.
5.7x28 mm SS195LF Ammo
The 5.7x28 SS195LF (Lead Free) is an FN Herstal sporting cartridge with a lightweight 1.77 g (27 grain) lead-free expanding bullet and aluminum core. It offers high muzzle velocity, up to about 720 m/s, and low weight, reducing recoil and lead contamination on shooting ranges.
5.7x28 mm SB193 Ammo
The 5.7x28 SB193 is a subsonic cartridge developed by FN Herstal for suppressed weapons such as the P90 and Five-seveN. Its bullet remains below the speed of sound, eliminating the loud supersonic crack.
9x21 mm PS Ammo
9x21 mm Ammo
The 9x21 mm PS cartridge (SP-10, GRAU index 7N29) is a Russian special-purpose pistol round with an enhanced armor-piercing bullet. It was developed by TsNIITochMash in the first half of the 1990s for the Gyurza weapon family, including the SR-1 and Udav pistols, to engage targets wearing personal body armor.
9x21 mm SP-10T Ammo
The Russian 9x21 mm SP-10T cartridge is a special high-penetration tracer round. It is intended for accurate engagement of enemy personnel wearing high-grade body armor.
9x21 mm PE Ammo
The 9x21 mm SP-12 pistol cartridge, often described as a high-efficiency expanding round or PE, was developed by TsNIITochMash in the 1990s for the Gyurza weapon system, including the SR-1 pistol and SR-2 Veresk submachine gun. Its main purpose is to maximize stopping and terminal effect against unarmored targets while reducing the risk of ricochet.
9x21 mm IMI Ammo
The 9x21 IMI is an Israeli pistol cartridge created in the late 1980s by Israel Military Industries. It was developed for civilian markets in countries where military-caliber 9x19 Parabellum weapons were restricted. Its ballistics and power are close to 9x19, but it uses a longer 21 mm case.
9x21 mm BT Ammo
The 9x21 mm BT cartridge (SP-13, GRAU index 7BT3) is a Russian special-purpose pistol round with an armor-piercing tracer bullet, adopted in 2000. It is intended for target indication, fire correction, and engagement of personnel wearing body armor at ranges up to 100 meters.
9x21 mm 7N42 Ammo
The Russian 9x21 mm 7N42 pistol cartridge, using an enhanced-penetration bullet, was developed under the Udav program for the 9 mm RG128 Udav self-loading pistol. It is intended to defeat personnel wearing body armor at increased ranges.
.45 ACP Ammo
.45 Ammo
The .45 ACP (Automatic Colt Pistol) is a famous American 11.43x23 mm pistol cartridge created by John Browning in 1904. Its heavy bullet delivers strong stopping power and normally travels at subsonic velocity, making the cartridge well suited for suppressed fire.
.45 FMJ Ammo
The .45 FMJ cartridge uses a Full Metal Jacket bullet and is a classic American pistol round. The bullet is about 11.43 mm in diameter, weighs roughly 14.9 grams (230 grains), and has a muzzle velocity of around 260 m/s.
.45 Hydra-Shok Ammo
.45 Hydra-Shok ammunition by Federal Premium is a well-known hollow-point load designed for self-defense and law-enforcement use. Its bullet features a central post and specially cut jacket that promote controlled expansion on impact and transfer energy to the target while reducing overpenetration.
.45 JHP Ammo
.45 JHP ammunition uses Jacketed Hollow Point expanding bullets. The hollow cavity in the nose causes the bullet to expand into a mushroom shape in soft tissue, increasing its diameter, improving stopping effect, and reducing the risk of overpenetration.
.45 AP Ammo
The .45 AP (Armor-Piercing) is an experimental type of .45 ACP (11.43x23 mm) ammunition. Because of the cartridge's relatively low bullet velocity, true armor-piercing versions with hard cores are not commonly mass-produced.
.45 M26 Ammo
The .45 M26 cartridge, officially Cartridge, Tracer, Caliber .45, M26 and previously developed as the T30, is a special American .45-caliber pistol cartridge with a tracer bullet. It was adopted in 1946 from a World War II-era design for target indication, fire correction, and signaling from submachine guns and other .45-caliber weapons.
.357 Magnum HP Ammo
.357 Ammo
The .357 Magnum HP (Hollow Point) is a powerful expanding-bullet cartridge designed to open up on impact for maximum terminal effect.
.357 Magnum SP Ammo
.357 Magnum SP (Soft Point) ammunition uses a semi-jacketed bullet with an exposed lead core at the nose. Controlled expansion in soft tissue provides a strong stopping effect.
.357 Magnum FMJ Ammo
The .357 Magnum FMJ (Full Metal Jacket) is a powerful 9x33mmR revolver cartridge with a fully jacketed bullet, commonly used for training, sport shooting, and weapons handling practice.
.357 Remington MAX Ammo
The .357 Remington Maximum (.357 Max) is a powerful super-magnum handgun cartridge created in 1983 by Remington and Ruger. It is based on a .357 Magnum case lengthened by 7.6 mm to hold more propellant and achieve higher velocity at longer ranges.
.44 Magnum HP Ammo
.44 Ammo
.44 Magnum HP (Hollow Point) ammunition uses powerful expanding hollow-point bullets. On impact the bullet expands and increases in diameter, creating a wider wound channel and strong stopping effect.
.44 Magnum JSP Ammo
.44 Magnum JSP (Jacketed Soft Point) ammunition uses bullets with an exposed lead nose and a metal jacket around the body. It provides strong stopping power with controlled expansion after impact.
.44 Magnum FMJ Ammo
.44 Magnum FMJ (Full Metal Jacket) ammunition uses fully jacketed bullets for heavy revolvers and hunting carbines. It offers deep penetration, resists deformation on impact, and is suitable for training and penetrating dense barriers.
.44 WCF Ammo
The .44 WCF (Winchester Center Fire), also known as .44 Winchester, was introduced by Winchester Repeating Arms Company in 1873. It is a famous American centerfire cartridge with a bottleneck case and became one of the first commercially successful cartridges usable in both rifles and revolvers.
5.45x39 mm PS Ammo
5.45x39 mm Ammo
The 5.45x39 PS cartridge (GRAU index 7N6 / 7N6M) is a standard Soviet and Russian intermediate round with a steel-core ball bullet, adopted in 1974 for the AK-74, AKS-74U, RPK-74, and other weapons of this caliber.
5.45x39 mm T Ammo
The 5.45x39 T cartridge (GRAU index 7T3, with the modernized 7T3M variant) is a Soviet and Russian military tracer round intended for target indication, fire correction, and combat at ranges up to 800 meters.
5.45x39 mm HP Ammo
5.45x39 mm expanding ammunition, usually using HP (Hollow Point) bullets, has a partially jacketed projectile with a cavity in the nose. On impact with soft tissue the bullet expands rapidly, increasing in diameter for high energy transfer and strong stopping effect in hunting or sport shooting.
5.45x39 mm US Ammo
The 5.45x39 US cartridge (reduced velocity, GRAU index 7U1) is a special subsonic round. It was designed for quiet, low-flash fire from rifles such as the AKS-74UB in the Kanareyka system when used with a suppressor.
5.45x39 mm BS Ammo
The 5.45x39 BS cartridge (GRAU index 7N24) is a Russian military round with a special armor-piercing bullet containing a heavy tungsten-carbide hard core. It is intended to defeat personnel wearing heavy body armor and lightly armored vehicles.
5.45x39 mm BP Ammo
The 5.45x39 BP cartridge (GRAU index 7N22) is a Russian enhanced-penetration armor-piercing round adopted in 1998. It is intended to defeat personnel in heavy body armor as well as unarmored vehicles.
5.56x45 mm M193 Ammo
5.56x45 mm Ammo
The 5.56x45 M193 was the first standard low-impulse intermediate cartridge used by the U.S. military and NATO countries, entering service in 1964. It uses a lightweight 55-grain (3.56 g) FMJ lead-core bullet with a muzzle velocity of about 990 m/s.
5.56x45 mm M856 Ammo
The 5.56x45 M856 is a standard NATO tracer cartridge introduced in the 1980s for target indication, fire correction, and shooting in poor visibility. Its trajectory is designed to closely match the standard M855 cartridge.
5.56x45 mm M855A1 Ammo
The 5.56x45 mm M855A1 Enhanced Performance Round (EPR) is a standard high-performance U.S. Army cartridge adopted to replace the conventional M855 round and improve armor penetration and consistency against targets.
5.56x45 mm M196 Ammo
The 5.56x45 mm M196 is a standard American tracer cartridge developed during the Vietnam War era. It was intended for target indication and real-time fire correction, with ballistics matched to the standard M193 ball cartridge.
5.56x45 mm M995 Ammo
The 5.56x45 mm M995 is a specialized U.S. military armor-piercing cartridge adopted in 1996. It is designed to engage targets wearing personal body armor and lightly armored vehicles.
5.56x45 mm Mk.262 Ammo
The 5.56x45 mm Mk 262 is a high-accuracy, high-performance cartridge developed by Black Hills Ammunition for U.S. special operations forces. It uses a heavy 77-grain (5 g) OTM (Open Tip Match) bullet, significantly improving accuracy and terminal performance from short-barreled carbines such as the M4 at extended ranges.
7.62x39 mm PS Ammo
7.62x39 mm Ammo
The 7.62x39 PS cartridge (GRAU index 57-N-231) is a Soviet 1943-pattern intermediate round with a standard steel-core bullet. It was designed to engage enemy personnel in the open or behind light cover and became the basic ammunition for AK/AKM rifles and SKS carbines.
7.62x39 mm T-45M Ammo
The 7.62 mm 1943-pattern cartridge with the modernized T-45M tracer bullet (GRAU index 57-T-231PM1, adopted in 2002) is intended for target indication, fire correction, and engagement of personnel from AK/AKM rifles, RPK machine guns, and SKS carbines at ranges up to 850 meters. The bullet tip is painted green.
7.62x39 mm PP Ammo
The 7.62x39 PP cartridge (GRAU index 7N27) is a Soviet/Russian intermediate round with an enhanced-penetration bullet, intended to engage enemy personnel including targets protected by helmets and body armor.
7.62x39 mm BZ Ammo
The 7.62 mm 1943-pattern cartridge with a BZ armor-piercing incendiary bullet (GRAU index 57-BZ-231) was developed to damage lightly armored vehicles, ignite fuel behind barriers, and engage personnel behind light cover at ranges up to 300 meters.
7.62x39 mm US Ammo
The 7.62x39 US cartridge (GRAU index 57-N-231U) is a specialized Soviet subsonic intermediate round with reduced bullet velocity. It was adopted in 1962 for covert and quiet fire from Kalashnikov rifles such as the AKM and AKSM when used with PBS or PBS-1 suppressors.
7.62x39 mm SP Ammo
A hunting cartridge with a semi-jacketed expanding soft-point bullet and an exposed lead core at the nose. On impact the bullet rapidly mushrooms, increases in diameter, and transfers maximum energy for reliable effect on medium game.
9x39 mm PAB-9 Ammo
9x39 mm Ammo
The 9x39 mm PAB-9 is a standard cartridge developed for special rifles and assault weapons such as the VSS Vintorez, AS Val, SR-3 Vikhr, OTs-14 Groza, and similar systems.
9x39 mm PAB-9 Ammo
The 9x39 mm PAB-9 is a standard cartridge developed for special rifles and assault weapons such as the VSS Vintorez, AS Val, SR-3 Vikhr, OTs-14 Groza, and similar systems.
9x39 mm SP-6 Ammo
The SP-6 cartridge is armor-piercing ammunition intended to engage targets behind barriers or protected by body armor.
9x39 mm SP-6 Ammo
The SP-6 cartridge is armor-piercing ammunition intended to engage targets behind barriers or protected by body armor.
9x39 mm SP-5 Ammo
The 9x39 mm SP-5 cartridge was developed in the mid-1980s and is better suited for engaging unarmored targets at medium range.
9x39 mm SP-5 Ammo
The 9x39 mm SP-5 cartridge was developed in the mid-1980s and is better suited for engaging unarmored targets at medium range.
7.62x51 mm M80 Ammo
7.62x51 mm Ammo
The standard 7.62x51 mm NATO M80 Ball cartridge is a common NATO rifle round with an approximately 9.5-gram Full Metal Jacket bullet, designed for battle rifles, machine guns, and designated-marksman systems.
7.62x51 mm M80 Ammo
7.62x51 mm NATO M80 is a standard military cartridge with a Full Metal Jacket ball bullet.
7.62x51 mm M61 Ammo
7.62x51 mm NATO M61 is a military cartridge with an armor-piercing bullet.
7.62x51 mm NATO M61 AP Ammo
The 7.62x51 mm M62 is a standard NATO military rifle cartridge with a tracer bullet. It is intended for target indication, real-time fire correction, and target marking during low-light or nighttime shooting.
7.62x54 mm LPS Ammo
7.62x54 mm Ammo
The 7.62x54R LPS cartridge, whose designation means light steel-core bullet, is a Soviet rifle and machine-gun round designed to engage personnel and light cover.
7.62x54 mm T-46 Ammo
The 7.62x54 mm T-46 tracer cartridge (GRAU index 7T2; early brass-case variants were indexed 57-T-322 and bimetal-case versions 57-T-323) is intended for target indication, fire correction, and engagement of personnel at ranges up to 1,000 meters. The bullet leaves a bright visible tracer path in flight, day or night.
7.62x54 mm SNB Ammo
The 7.62x54 SNB cartridge (sniper armor-piercing, GRAU index 7N14) is a Russian sniper round developed in the 1990s to improve the effectiveness of the SVD against targets wearing modern body armor.
7.62x54 mm LPS Ammo
The 7.62x54 mm LPS (57-N-223S-01) is a cartridge with a light LPS steel-core bullet.
7.62x54 mm PP Ammo
The 7.62x54 PP cartridge (GRAU index 7N13 with a bimetal case or 7N13-01 with a steel case) is a Soviet/Russian rifle and machine-gun round with an enhanced-penetration bullet. It was developed in the mid-1990s to defeat personnel wearing body armor and lightly armored vehicles.
7.62x54 mm SNB Ammo
The 7.62x54 mm SNB (7N14) is a sniper armor-piercing cartridge.
7.62x67 mm FMJ Ammo
7.62x67 mm Ammo
The 7.62x67 mm cartridge, better known as .300 Winchester Magnum (.300 Win Mag), is available with FMJ bullets mainly for training, precision sport shooting, and military or police sniping, including tactical loads such as SWISS P Ball.
7.62x67 mm PRC Ammo
7.62x67 mm PRC (Precision Rifle Cartridge) ammunition, developed by Hornady, represents a family of modern rimless, beltless magnum cartridges. The line is designed for extreme long-range precision shooting and hunting with long, heavy, high-ballistic-coefficient bullets.
12.7x55 mm PS12 Ammo
The 12.7x55 mm PS-12 is a special Russian large-caliber cartridge with a heavy 33-gram subsonic bullet. It was developed in the early 2010s for the ASh-12 assault weapon system and RSh-12 revolver, providing very high stopping power against personnel at short range.
12.7x55 mm VPS Ammo
The 12.7x55 mm STs-130 VPS high-penetration cartridge is a special Russian large-caliber round developed by TsKIB SOO for the VSSK Vykhlop suppressed sniper rifle and ASh-12 assault rifle. It is intended to defeat targets in heavy body armor or behind light cover at ranges up to 600 meters while retaining a low-signature firing profile.
12.7x55 mm PS12B Ammo
The 12.7x55 mm PS12B is a special Russian large-caliber cartridge with an armor-piercing bullet containing a heat-treated steel core. It was developed for assault weapons such as the ASh-12 and RSh-12 for special operations at short and medium ranges, combining strong stopping power with penetration of heavy armor.
12.7x55 mm PT2 Ammo
The 12.7x55 mm STs-130 PT2 is a Russian high-precision sniper cartridge with a solid bronze bullet, developed by TsKIB SOO in 2004. It is intended to engage unarmored personnel at ranges up to 600 meters.
12x70 Slug Ammo
12x70 Ammo
A 12x70 cartridge with a zhekan is a standard 12-gauge, 70 mm smoothbore shell loaded with a solid slug. The Russian term zhekan, also written zhakan, is a traditional name for a slug derived from an early projectile design. Such ammunition is used for hunting large game and shooting at medium distances.
12x70 Armor-Piercing Slug Ammo
A 12x70 shell with an armor-piercing 12-gauge slug featuring lead driving bands and a heat-treated brass core. It can penetrate medium body armor while retaining very high stopping power.
12x70 Birdshot Ammo
A 12x70 hunting shell loaded with shot is one of the most common standard loads for 12-gauge smoothbore weapons with a 70 mm chamber. The 12 indicates the gauge and 70 the case length in millimeters. A typical shot charge weighs about 28-32 grams, with muzzle velocity around 190-210 m/s.
12x70 Buckshot Ammo
A 12x70 buckshot shell is a standard 70 mm smoothbore cartridge loaded with large lead pellets roughly 5.6-8.5 mm in diameter. It delivers strong stopping power and is intended for medium game at ranges of about 35-50 meters.
12x70 Flechette Ammo
A 12x70 flechette shell is a 12-gauge smoothbore cartridge loaded with small metal darts instead of conventional shot or buckshot.
12x70 Sabot Dart Ammo
A custom 12x70 shell loaded with a fin-stabilized steel dart instead of a conventional slug. The smoothbore shotgun barrel allows this projectile design to be used effectively, providing high accuracy and armor penetration, though the complexity of manufacture makes this improvised cartridge uncommon.
23x75 mm Shrapnel-10 Ammo
23x75 mm Ammo
The 23x75 mm Shrapnel-10 is a special buckshot cartridge for the KS-23 carbine, designed for short-range use out to about 10 meters.
23x75 mm Shrapnel-25 Ammo
The 23x75 mm Shrapnel-25 is a special buckshot cartridge intended for service use in weapons such as the KS-23. The number 25 in the name refers to the cartridge's maximum effective range in meters.
23x75 mm Barrikada Ammo
The 23x75 mm Barrikada is a special Soviet/Russian cartridge for the KS-23 carbine, loaded with a heavy pointed solid-steel projectile. It was designed to forcibly stop vehicles by damaging the engine or other critical components.
23x75 mm Signal Ammo
The 23x75 mm SP cartridge is a red signal round for the SPSh-44 flare pistol.
